newsitem.title: USA: H-P off after analyst's negative comments.
newsitem.headline: H-P off after analyst's negative comments.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co's shares fell at the opening of trading Friday following negative comments by Soundview analyst Russell Crabs about several of the company's businesses, traders said.
Shares of the diversified computer products supplier fell 1-1/4 to 56-1/2 in early trading Friday.
Later, Soundview confirmed that Crabs had cut his short-term rating on Hewlett-Packard to hold from buy, but maintained his long-term buy rating.
It said the analyst cut his 1997 fiscal year estimate to $3.22 per share by a penny from $3.23 per share and cut his fiscal 1998 estimate to $3.75 from $3.87 per share previously.
In addition, Prudential analyst Don Young cut his 1997 year estimate by a nickel to $3.35 a share from $3.40 previously, in what his office said was "just an adjustment."
The prior Wall Street consensus for Hewlett's 1997 fiscal year ending in October was $3.22 per share while the 1998 year consensus was $3.67 per share, according to First Call.

In the firm's morning meeting, Crabs raised concerns about order flow in printers and the possibility of an extended product transition in its server business ahead of the release of the next-generation micrprocessor technology Hewlett is developing with Intel Corp known as Merced, a market source said.

He also cited a downturn in the computermaker's customer satisfaction as measured in a Soundview-commissioned survey, the source said. The analyst was not immediately available to confirm the comments.
However, Gruntal analyst Mona Eraiba said she believed the stock's decline Friday was a buying opportunity.

She said the transition to Merced-based microprocessors was a distant event that was not likely to occur before late in 1998. "Merced is a big positive. It is not going to be a destructive event," she said. Eraiba maintains a strong buy.
